title: A Son from Your Own Body

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the word of the Lord came to him: "This man will not be your heir, but a son who is your own flesh and blood will be your heir." - Gen 15:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abram had a sensible backup plan. If God wouldn't give him a son, he'd make his servant Eliezer the heir. It was reasonable, legal, and it solved the problem. And God says: no. "This man will not be your heir."

God refuses Abram's workaround. Not because the plan was wicked, but because it was too small. God had something better in mind - "a son who is your own flesh and blood." Abram was settling for a legal arrangement when God intended a miracle.

How often we do this. Faced with a delay, we construct our own solution - sensible, practical, achievable. And sometimes God graciously says no, because our workaround would rob us of what He actually intends to give.

This isn't a promise that God always says yes to our biggest dreams; sometimes His better plan looks nothing like ours. But it does mean we can trust Him when He closes off our clever alternatives. Paul writes that God "is able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine" (Eph 3:20). When God blocks your Eliezer plan, it may be because He has a son in mind. Don't settle for a workaround when God intends a miracle.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you settled for a workaround where God intended something better?
- Can you trust God when He closes off your sensible alternatives?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, forgive me for settling for my own small solutions. When You close off my workarounds, help me trust that You have something better in mind. Enlarge my expectation of You.
Amen.
